content.text:
Good corrections — these change real parts of the plan. Updating accordingly.

## Changes to the plan

**Fjaerland** moves out of any resume-style framing entirely (there wasn't a formal "experience" list on this site anyway) and becomes a short, honest aside in the "where it comes from" section, alongside her grandmother and the books: a ten-week unpaid stage — washing jars, labelling, helping on two garum batches. No "researcher," no lab-credential language.

**The waste section** now reads as "we," not "I" — whole kitchen, prep and plate waste only, measured over one month in 2023, bones excluded because they go to stock. That's a meaningful rewrite of the copy, not a word swap.

**Head Chef date**: site says September 2022, full stop. I'm assuming you want the acting-head-chef period (March–September 2022) left out entirely rather than footnoted — tell me if you'd rather it got a quiet mention somewhere.

**New section: how the kitchen runs.** I'm adding this before the larder — the prep list and the ferment log (start date, salt %, check days, ready date) as the actual operating system of the kitchen, with the line that the menu is written last, not first. This also fixes the larder section: jar labels in that section will show real log fields instead of vague invented notes. I'll need a handful of real examples from you for this — I don't want to fabricate plausible-sounding salt percentages and dates, since made-up specifics would undercut exactly the authenticity this section is for.

**Photo and face rules, built into the plan, not just noted:**
- Priya's photos get her credit line wherever they appear. I'm assuming Saltmarsh/Priya are fine with portfolio reuse on your say-so, but that's worth a direct confirmation from Callum or Priya before launch — a restaurant owning photos and a restaurant being fine with them on your personal site aren't automatically the same thing.
- Olu's drawings are treated as **not yet cleared**. The Brine section is designed to stand on its own using zine covers and your own photos of the physical issues, so it doesn't depend on his drawings existing — his illustrations become an upgrade slotted in later if he says yes, not a dependency now.
- No staff faces anywhere by default. The apprentices/Sunday Pot section uses hands, prep action, backs — not faces — until you tell me specific people and photos are cleared.
- No pricing anywhere, supplier or otherwise (this was never planned, just confirming).

**Audience and tone, which reshapes the closing section specifically.** You're not job-hunting, so the whole site already avoided a CV/resume shape — this makes that explicit. The closing section's three calls-to-action become: apply to the apprentice programme, press/writer contact, and book a workshop. Nothing anywhere should read as "hire me." Still need from you: how apprentices actually apply, how workshops get booked, and what contact method you want listed — these three are the last real content gaps before this is buildable.

Let me know on the open points (the ferment-log examples, the Priya/restaurant check, apprentice/workshop/contact mechanics), and I'll fold the answers in before we talk about building anything.

---
name: storyfolio-chef-site-plan
description: Scroll narrative, visual language, and mobile plan for Ines Okafor's chef portfolio site (not a dev/designer template)
metadata:
  type: project
---

Concept: "the larder" — scrolling mirrors walking through Ines's larder/fermentation process (patience, transformation of trim into the menu), not a resume. All motion/3D ideas must tie to real kitchen objects (jars, labels, steam, brine, paper) rather than abstract geometric/WebGL-demo motion — the test is "could this be swapped onto any chef's name," and if yes it's wrong.

Scroll order (current, revised after [[ines-okafor-portfolio-facts]] corrections):
1. Jar wall hero (Priya Nair photo, layered parallax, name/title fade in low)
2. Intro — "most of what I care about happens before service" over a focusing prep photo
3. How the kitchen runs — prep list + ferment log (start date, salt %, check days, ready date); menu is written last, not first. New section added to anchor authenticity of larder labels.
4. The larder — 40+ ferments as a shelf, scroll-linked horizontal move on desktop, swipeable gallery on mobile; jar labels show real ferment-log fields, not invented notes
5. Before/after waste transition — scrubbed split image, copy as "we," prep+plate only, one month in 2023, bones excluded
6. The koji room — deliberately small/dark, it's a cupboard
7. People — apprentices + Sunday Pot; no staff faces by default, hands/action shots only; Callum Reyes pull-quote here
8. Brine the zine — page-flip interaction using zine covers/physical-issue photos; Olu's drawings are an optional upgrade, not a dependency
9. Where it comes from — grandmother's ogiri pot + the two fermentation books + Fjaerland stage as a humble lineage aside (not a credential)
10. Visit/contact — three CTAs only: apply to apprentice programme, press/writer contact, book a workshop. No "hire me" framing anywhere.

Visual language:
- Palette: jar amber, deep olive, bone/cream, charcoal (not pure black), sparing koji-green accent. No neon/gradient-for-effect.
- Type: editorial/printed-feel serif for headings (sympathy with the Brine zine), plain warm sans for body/UI, hand-lettered face reserved only for jar labels themselves.

Mobile: vertical scroll stays primary driver (most traffic expected via Instagram/search, phone-first). Horizontal larder shelf becomes swipeable gallery; scrubbed before/after becomes simple swap; max two parallax layers; respect prefers-reduced-motion; images need real responsive sizing + lazy-load given 60+ photos.

Status as of 2026-10-10: plan stage only, nothing built yet. Waiting on open content gaps listed in [[ines-okafor-portfolio-facts]] before building.
